failure: Failure: It does not refute the Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture, does not show that every coordinate in F_m is bad, and does not disprove existence of some coordinate with Δ_i≤C I_i. It only rules out an all-coordinate linear decrement inequality. The equality statement is one-way: upper-bound equality is possible only at influences 0, 1/2, or 1; influence 1/2 alone is not sufficient.
interface: Interface: All quantities use the source’s Boolean Fourier normalization. The theorem concerns a specified coordinate; the family need not have every coordinate bad.

claims.title: Boolean coordinate restriction has a sharp entropy modulus, but a prescribed-coordinate ratio diverges
